You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

"225 :     public void parseFromCentralDirectoryData(
226 :             byte[] buffer, int offset, int length
227 :     ) throws ZipException {
228 :     }"

Diagnosis:
The test method testParseReparse tests the parsing and reparsing of extra Unix fields in zip archives, specifically the "ux" extra field encoded by the class X7875_NewUnix. The test defines multiple sample byte arrays representing different encoded values of version, UID and GID. It calls the helper parseReparse method which does an initial parse of the "local file data" field bytes to decode the UID and GID, checks that the decoded values match expectations, then marshals back to bytes using getLocalFileDataData, and reparses those bytes to verify no state corruption.

The exception reported in the current bug report is an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in X7875_NewUnix.parseFromLocalFileData when parsing a 0-sized ux local entry. Looking at the parseFromLocalFileData method reveals the root cause:

- It first reads the version byte.
- Next, it reads uidSize, which is treated as an unsigned int.
- Then it copies uidSize bytes from data into a uidBytes array.
- Next it increments offset by uidSize.
- Now it reads gidSize from data.
- Copies gidSize bytes into gidBytes.
- Finally it sets gid/GID BigIntegers from these reversed byte arrays.

This code assumes that the array has at least (1 + 1 + uidSize + 1 + gidSize) bytes not exceeding the available array. However, if the input byte array is of length 3 and encodes zero-length UID and GID fields (for example {1,0,0} which is ZERO_LEN in the test), then the offset+uidSize or offset+gidSize copy operations exceed the array bounds (since uidSize and gidSize are zero it still attempts to copy 0 bytes, but offset++ and copy sequence lead to overrun).

There is no check in the code to verify that the offset + uidSize or offset + gidSize stay within the array length bounds before calling System.arraycopy. This causes the ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when a zero-length UID or GID field extra data is encountered.

This explains the excepting while parsing 0-sized "ux" local entry reported in the issue.

Supporting this is that the test explicitly defines the ZERO_LEN extra data and it is passed to parseReparse, where it calls parseFromLocalFileData. The failure happens in that low-level parse method when handling zero-length UID/GID fields.

Conclusion:
The failure occurs because parseFromLocalFileData does not perform adequate bounds checking on the input byte array when reading uidSize and gidSize fields and copying bytes. When those lengths are zero, the method tries to read out-of-range elements and triggers an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

The test and issue report match this scenario exactly.

No other recent bug reports appear directly relevant.

The fix requires adding length checks in parseFromLocalFileData to ensure it never reads past the provided data array length, especially taking into account zero-length UID/GID possible in version 1 entries. Possibly also early sanity checks for array size before parsing fields would be prudent.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
